name: Modmail
author: contact@velrix.net
description: A shared inbox for your Discord server. Members DM the bot to open a private thread your whole staff team can read and reply to. Needs a MongoDB database, which the free MongoDB Atlas tier covers.
startup: export PIP_USER=1; export PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1; export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1; export USING_DOCKER=yes; export PATH=/home/container/.local/bin:$PATH; for v in MODMAIL_GUILD_ID OWNERS LOG_URL; do [[ -z "${!v:-}" ]] && unset "$v"; done; if [[ "{{AUTO_UPDATE}}" == "1" ]] && [[ -d .git ]]; then echo "Checking for a Modmail update..."; if git pull -q --ff-only --no-tags; then pip install -q -U -r requirements.txt; else echo "Update skipped: local changes or a diverged branch. Booting the installed version."; fi; fi; python bot.py

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Modmail installation
#
# Server files: /mnt/server at install time, /home/container at run time.

set -euo pipefail

MODMAIL_BRANCH="${MODMAIL_BRANCH:-master}"
REPO="https://github.com/modmail-dev/Modmail.git"

# -qq plus noninteractive: apt's per-package Unpacking/Setting up chatter is
# most of this log and nobody reads it. Errors still print.
echo "Installing prerequisites..."
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get -qq update
apt-get -qq install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates

# The volume belongs to the node's container user and this script runs as root,
# so git calls the repository "dubious ownership" and refuses every command
# against it. That check exists to stop root being tricked into running hooks
# from a directory someone else controls; here we mounted the directory
# ourselves and root is what the installer is supposed to be, so the exception
# is the correct answer rather than a workaround.
#
# Set through the environment rather than `git config --global`, because HOME is
# repointed at the volume a few lines down and git's "global" config follows
# HOME. Writing it to /root/.gitconfig first would leave it somewhere git stops
# reading, which fails exactly like having never set it.
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1
export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory
export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/mnt/server

# --user installs resolve .local against $HOME at run time, which is the one
# thing that differs between this container and the runtime one: /mnt/server
# here, /home/container there. It is the same directory on the same volume, so
# pointing HOME at it now puts every package exactly where the bot will look
# for it later. A venv could not do this -- it hardcodes its own path.
#
# The path it lands in is .local/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages, so this image's
# Python MINOR version has to match the runtime yolk's or the bot boots into an
# empty site-packages. That is why the egg pins exactly one docker image: adding
# a Python 3.12 option without changing this container is a silent break.
export HOME=/mnt/server
mkdir -p "${HOME}"
cd "${HOME}"

# git init + fetch rather than git clone, because clone refuses a non-empty
# directory and this script has to survive a reinstall over an existing server.
# checkout -f overwrites whatever is tracked; plugins/, config.json and .env are
# all gitignored upstream, so a user's own files and settings survive it.
echo "Fetching Modmail (${MODMAIL_BRANCH})..."
if [ ! -d .git ]; then
    git init -q .
fi
if git remote | grep -qx origin; then
    git remote set-url origin "${REPO}"
else
    git remote add origin "${REPO}"
fi
git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "${MODMAIL_BRANCH}"
git checkout -qf -B "${MODMAIL_BRANCH}" "origin/${MODMAIL_BRANCH}"
# Give the branch an upstream so the AUTO_UPDATE git pull at boot has somewhere
# to pull from. A shallow checkout deepens itself on the next fetch, which is
# fine -- the alternative is a bare "there is no tracking information" failure.
git branch -q --set-upstream-to="origin/${MODMAIL_BRANCH}" "${MODMAIL_BRANCH}"
echo "Checked out $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)."

# --root-user-action=ignore: the installer container IS root by design, so pip's
# warning is advice for a situation that cannot arise here.
# --no-cache-dir: HOME is the server volume, so the cache would be written into
# the user's own files and count against their disk, for a cache no later
# install can read since this container is discarded.
# --progress-bar off: nothing watches this log while it streams.
# --disable-pip-version-check: "a new release of pip is available" is advice for
# someone with a shell, and this container is gone by the time anyone reads it.
PIP_FLAGS="--user --upgrade --no-warn-script-location --root-user-action=ignore --progress-bar off --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check"

echo "Installing Python dependencies..."

# Drop the image's preinstalled wheel first. It is the only package here that
# declares a dependency on packaging, it wants >= 24, and upstream's lockfile
# pins packaging 23.2 -- so leaving it installed ends every successful install
# with a red pip conflict about two packages Modmail never imports. Nothing
# needs it: two of the requirements are sdists, and pip builds those in an
# isolated environment where it installs its own copy of wheel.
#
# Removing the cause rather than passing --no-warn-conflicts, so a conflict
# among Modmail's own dependencies would still be reported.
python -m pip uninstall -y --root-user-action=ignore -q wheel

# pip itself is deliberately not upgraded. Every requirement below is pinned to
# an exact version by upstream's lockfile, so a newer resolver has nothing to
# decide, and a --user pip would put ~15 MB of tooling on the server's disk
# quota to do it.
python -m pip install ${PIP_FLAGS} -r requirements.txt

# A wheel that silently failed to land shows up at boot as a traceback on a
# server nobody is watching, so fail here instead, while the log is on screen.
# cairosvg is deliberately NOT imported: it dlopens libcairo, which this image
# does not carry and the runtime yolk does, so a check here would fail for the
# wrong reason. Modmail hard-exits at boot when that import fails, so the yolk
# the egg runs on has to keep carrying libcairo.so.2, libpango and gdk-pixbuf.
echo "Verifying the install..."
python - <<'PYCHECK'
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/mnt/server")
import discord  # noqa: F401
import motor  # noqa: F401

print(f"discord.py {discord.__version__}")
PYCHECK

mkdir -p "${HOME}/plugins"

# Everything above was written by root, and the server runs as the node's
# container user, which cannot write to root-owned files. The volume's own
# directory already carries the ownership the node wants, so copy it downward
# rather than guessing a uid. Wings does chown after an install, so on a healthy
# node this changes nothing; it costs one pass over the tree and removes a
# whole class of "permission denied" first boots if it ever does not.
echo "Handing the files to the server user..."
chown -R --reference=/mnt/server /mnt/server

echo
echo "Modmail install complete."
echo "Modmail will not start until CONNECTION_URI points at a MongoDB database."
exit 0

variables.name: Bot Token
variables.description: Your bot's token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot -> Reset Token). Turn on the Server Members and Message Content intents on the same page, or the bot will not start.

variables.name: Server ID
variables.description: The ID of the Discord server this bot handles modmail for. Turn on Developer Mode in Discord, then right-click the server and Copy Server ID.

variables.name: MongoDB Connection URI
variables.description: Where Modmail stores its threads, logs and settings. There is no database inside this server, so point it at a MongoDB you control. A free MongoDB Atlas cluster is what the Modmail docs recommend. Allow access from any IP on the Atlas side, since this server's address can change.

variables.name: Bot Owners
variables.description: Discord user IDs allowed to run owner-only commands, separated by commas and nothing else. Leave empty to allow only the bot's application owner.

variables.name: Staff Server ID
variables.description: Only for the two-server setup, where threads are created in a separate staff server. Leave empty to keep everything in the server above.

variables.name: Log Viewer URL
variables.description: The address of your Modmail log viewer, if you run one. Leave empty and thread logs are still saved, the links posted in Discord just will not open anywhere.

variables.name: Update On Boot
variables.description: Pull the latest Modmail each time the server starts. It is skipped automatically if you have edited the bot's own files.

variables.name: Modmail Branch
variables.description: Which branch to install. master is the stable one. Changing this only takes effect when the server is reinstalled.
